title: direwolf.tool.result v6
description: A version-6 invocation whose whole plan was allowed, performed, and recorded.

ActionDecision.description: How the two gates of ADR-0006 decided one action of a plan.

effect.description: What was decided for this action.

capability_result.description: Whether a held capability covers the action.

rule_id.description: The rule that produced the effect, or could not be evaluated.

ContentRevision.description:
A file revision, stated exactly: the SHA-256 of its whole content and
its length. Objectively checkable; no timestamp, no version-control
system, no claim the file cannot confirm.

ExecutableRef.description:
An executable's authority identity: where it resolved to, and what was
there. Two builds of the same program at the same path are two
identities.

path.description:
The canonical host path of the final object: every symlink on the
way resolved, no symlink left on it.

sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the file's whole content, from the descriptor the
authority opened and hashed.

FsDeleteResult.description: An `fs.delete` completed: the name no longer exists.

FsListEntry.description: One entry of a directory listing.

name.description: Its name: one canonical path component.

kind.description: What the directory says it is. Not followed or opened.

FsListResult.description:
What an `fs.list` returned. The broker examined the first `max_entries`
names in byte order; the addressable ones are listed, and the ones no
canonical path can name — not UTF-8, not NFC, or holding a control,
bidi or invisible-format character — are counted and never emitted.

entries.description: The addressable entries, in ascending byte order.

unaddressable.description: How many of the examined entries could not be named.

complete.description: Whether every entry of the directory was examined.

FsMoveResult.description:
An `fs.move` completed: the source name no longer exists and the
destination name binds the object that was checked.

post.description: The file's revision now: the patch's post revision.

content.description:
The bytes read from the start of the file, exactly, as hexadecimal.
At most the call's `max_bytes`; their count is the content's
length, and is not repeated.

eof_observed.description:
Whether the end of the file was **observed** during this read: a
read returned no bytes before `max_bytes` were read. `false` when
exactly `max_bytes` were read — the end was then not proven, because
finding it would have meant reading past the authorised bound, and
the broker never does (ADR-0043).

FsSearchResult.description: What an `fs.search` returned: offsets, never content.

offsets.description:
Every offset at which the needle starts and ends within the scanned
bytes, overlapping occurrences included, up to `max_matches`.

scanned.description: How many bytes were scanned: at most `max_scan_bytes`, never more.

eof_observed.description: Whether the end of the file was observed within the scan.

matches_truncated.description: Whether more matches were found than were returned.

FsStatResult.description: What an `fs.stat` returned, from the checked object's own descriptor.

size.description:
`st_size`: a regular file's length; for a directory, the
filesystem's size of the directory object, not of its contents.

executable.description:
Whether a regular file has any execute bit. Always false for a
directory.

created.description: Whether the file did not exist and was created.

HttpHeader.description: One header: a name and a value, each in its one spelling.

ImageExecutableRef.description:
An executable in an image: the identity a sandboxed launch is decided
on. The image is content addressed and its root read-only, so the path
names one file in every environment made from it; the broker proves
that file's bytes against `sha256` before every launch.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 the operator's manifest pins for it.

NetActionDecision.description: How the gates decided one network or injection action.

capability_result.description: Whether a held capability covers the action.

rule_id.description: The rule that produced the effect, or could not be evaluated.

NetHop.description:
One hop of a `net.http`: where it went and what came back. No path, no
query, no header, no address.

status.description: The status the response carried, if one arrived.

injected.description: Whether a credential was injected into this hop.

NetHttpResult.description:
What a `net.http` brought back: the last response's status, its kept
headers and its body — redacted of every configured secret value, and
cut at the bound — and every hop.

headers.description:
Its headers on the keep-list (`crate::wire::http`), `location` as
the authority canonicalised it. Never `set-cookie`.

body.description: Its body, as lowercase hexadecimal: at most the request's bound.

truncated.description: Whether the body was longer than what came back.

redirect_ended.description: Why a redirect the last response asked for was not followed.

PlannedAction.description:
One canonical action a call requires: every fact policy decided on,
stated by the authority. The capability it required is
`<verb>:<canonical_path>?max_bytes=<byte_count>&no_symlink_targets=true`
for `fs.read` and `fs.write`, and
`<verb>:<canonical_path>?no_symlink_targets=true` for the others.

canonical_path.description:
The object's canonical path: resolved beneath the pinned root, or —
for a vacant name — the checked parent's path and the validated
name.

object.description: Whether the object existed when it was resolved.

byte_count.description:
The file-content bytes the action reads or writes, which is what
policy's `max_bytes` bounds: the request's bound for a read or a
scan, the content's length for a write, zero for metadata and names.

decision.description: Both gates' decision for this action.

PlannedActionV6.description:
One action of a version-6 plan: exactly one of a filesystem action, a
host process action, a sandboxed launch, a network action, a hop's
injection and a launch's injection.

injection.description: A credential's injection into a `net.http` hop.

spawn_injection.description: A credential's injection into a sandboxed launch.

PlannedInjectionAction.description:
The injection action of a `net.http` hop that asked for a credential:
`secret.use:<handle>`, at exactly the hop's origin. The value is never
stated, nor its header, nor its length.

host.description: The origin's host it would be injected at.

PlannedNetAction.description:
The network action of a `net.http` hop: `network.https:<host>:<port>`
with `methods=<method>`, as the authority canonicalised it. Neither the
path nor the query is stated: the URL is named by its digest, so the
plan says which request it is without repeating what it carries.

url_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the canonical URL (`https://host:port/path?query`).

body_bytes.description: How many body bytes the request carries.

PlannedProcessAction.description:
One canonical process action: every fact policy decided on, stated by
the authority. The capability it required is
`<verb>:<executable path>@<sha256>` — with
`?argv_allowlist=<first argument>` for a launch whose first argument is
an allowlist token.

executable.description:
The executable identity it is about: for a launch, the one
resolved and hashed now; for a status or a kill, the one the process
was launched as.

process_id.description: The process, for a status or a kill.

cwd.description: The working directory's canonical path, for a launch.

arg_count.description: How many arguments follow `argv[0]`, for a launch.

argv_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the canonical argv — `argv[0]` and every argument —
for a launch: what an approval will bind (ADR-0045 §7).

argv_safety.description: The kernel's classification of the arguments, for a launch.

decision.description: Both gates' decision for this action.

PlannedSpawnInjectionAction.description:
The injection action of a sandboxed launch that consumes a
credential: `secret.use:<handle>`, environment `SANDBOX`, delivered to
the plan's workload executable in the mode stated. The value is never
stated, nor its length, nor the variable that would carry it.

mode.description: How it would reach the executable.

PlannedWorkloadAction.description:
One sandboxed launch, as the authority decided it: every fact policy
decided on (the environment is `SANDBOX`), the environment it chose,
and the bounds it will hold the launch to. The capability it required
is `process.exec:<path>@<sha256>` — with `?argv_allowlist=<first
argument>` for a first argument an allowlist can name.

environment_id.description:
The environment the authority chose: the run's `READY` one.
Absent from a denial, which needs none, and from a preview of a
run whose environment an invocation would prepare.

arg_count.description:
How many arguments follow `argv[0]`, as the broker is told them:
the obligation's first, then the call's.

argv_safety.description:
The kernel's classification of the call's arguments: what policy
decided on.

timeout_seconds.description: The wall clock it will be held to.

max_stream_bytes.description: How many bytes of each stream come back.

decision.description: Both gates' decision for this action.

ProcessActionDecision.description: How the gates decided one process action.

capability_result.description: Whether a held capability covers the action.

rule_id.description: The rule that produced the effect, or could not be evaluated.

ProcessExecResult.description:
What a `process.exec` did: the target executable replaced the broker's
launch helper — `execve` succeeded — and the broker supervises it.

state.description: What it was when the launch was confirmed.

exit_code.description: Its exit code, if it had already exited.

signal.description: The signal that ended it, if one already had.

exit_code.description: Its exit code, when it exited.

signal.description: The signal that ended it, when one did.

timed_out.description: Whether the broker ended it at its wall-clock bound.

ProcessStreamSnapshot.description:
One output stream, as the broker retained it: its **first** bytes, in
order, and how many it saw.

content.description:
The retained bytes: at most the launch's per-stream bound, and never
more than [`crate::limits::MAX_PROCESS_STREAM_BYTES`].

observed.description: Every byte the process wrote to the stream so far, retained or not.

truncated.description: Whether more was written than was retained.

SandboxedExecResult.description:
What a sandboxed `process.exec` did: where it ran, at what level, as
which executable, how it ended, its bounded output, and what the
environment's init found after it. Its output is content the
environment produced: the run is `LOCAL_UNVERIFIED` before this is
answered, and a configured secret's value in it is redacted.

executable.description: The executable, in the image, whose bytes the broker proved.

stdout.description: Its standard output, redacted, to the bound.

stderr.description: Its standard error, redacted, to the bound.

residue.description:
Whether every other process of the environment was then proved
gone.

ended_processes.description: How many processes, besides init, were found and ended.

environment_destroyed.description:
Whether the environment was destroyed after it: its residue was
not proved clean.

ToolOutputV5.description:
A version-5 tool's output: **exactly one** member, the call's own. A
`process_exec` in an execution environment answers with
`process_exec_sandboxed`; on the host, with `process_exec`.

process_status.description: A host process's state and output.

ToolPlanV6.description:
The canonical plan a version-6 call resolves to. `effect` is `ALLOW`
only if **every** action is allowed: a launch that consumes a
credential runs only if its workload action and its spawn injection
are both allowed.

effect.description: The decision for the whole call.

ToolResultV6.description:
A version-6 invocation every action of whose plan was allowed, which
the broker performed, and which the authority recorded. Its output is
version 5's: a launch that consumed a credential has its output
redacted of the value before this is answered.

invocation_id.description: The authority's id for this invocation.

plan.description: The plan that was decided and performed.
